title: No Kings- No Time to Celebrate
description:
On Flag Day Saturday June 14th, stand with us on the sidewalk at the corner of Maple Street and Lafayette Street (Route 114) in Marblehead from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m., for “No Kings- No Time to Celebrate” —a nonpartisan, peaceful stand out to stand up in defense of American democracy.

This is no time to celebrate. America is in a Constitutional crisis. 

The colors of the American flag have been described as “Red for courage and readiness to sacrifice; white for pure intentions and high ideals; and blue for vigilance and justice.” Our Veterans have fought and died to defend our flag and our values and we should not betray their sacrifice. 
On this Flag Day in 2025, we call on those same qualities of American spirit- courage and sacrifice, vigilance and justice- as we defend the pillars of democracy.  We refuse to celebrate when America is in a Constitutional crisis.

Come to this peaceful demonstration. Bring your signs, your friends, your determination—and your belief that the United States was never meant to have kings. Join us!

Organized by the Marblehead Alliance for Democracy.

Corporations are drowning out our voices! We need money out of politics. WE WANT ELECTED OFFICIALS TO REPRESENT THE PEOPLE, NOT CORPORATIONS!


**Join Michigan United Action in our TBOP committee meeting to see what's next for the campaign.** There are big changes coming up and we need all hands on deck. title: Sun. 6/8 > I-91 Overpass Standout - 9 Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Trying a Sunday standout again, for those who can't make our weekday afternoons. It's a kid-friendly space on a lightly traveled roadway. Let's make this thing GROW!!!

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

description:

In anticipation of this decision, we at Equality Michigan, along with our partners at the ACLU of Michigan, are offering this statewide virtual webinar to discuss the details and breadth of the decision, as well as how it does and does not impact Michiganders. 

The conversation will feature Emme Zanotti, Equality Michigan's Senior Director of Movement Building & Political Affairs; and Jay Kaplan, the ACLU of Michigan's LGBTQ+ Rights Project Staff Attorney.

There will be a Q&A portion of the webinar, where panelists can answer questions related both to the case, and to some other relevant issues impacting Michigan's LGBTQ+ community. 

In the event that a decision comes sooner in June, we may move this meeting up to more urgently answer your questions and try to address your concerns.
